simple.meaning: מַסָּה (Maççâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “Massah , a place in the Desert.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַסָּה (H4532) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 17:7, with occurrences in Exodus, Deuteronomy.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַסָּה (H4532) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַסָּה (H4532) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַסָּה (Maççâh) / H4532 is traced through Exodus 17:7, Deuteronomy 6:16, Deuteronomy 9:22, Deuteronomy 33:8 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Massah , a place in the Desert
definitions.full: H4532. Massah III. מַסָּה proper name, of a location where Israel tried ׳י in the wilderness, Exod 17:7 (JE), Deut 6:16 ; 9:22 ; Psa 95:8 (all ᵐ5 ( ὁ ) πειρασμός ), where Levi was tested Deut 33:8 ( ᵐ5 πείρᾳ ). **See Gall Kultstätten 32 interprets as place of trial (ancient judgment-place) and identification with Kadesh, called also מְרִיבָה (מֵי) and מִשְׁמָּט עֵין .

occurrences.englishText: He called the name of the place Massah,* Massah means testing. and Meribah,† Meribah means quarreling. because the children of Israel quarreled, and because they tested Yahweh, saying, “Is Yahweh among us, or not?”
You shall not tempt Yahweh your God, as you tempted him in Massah.
At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth Hattaavah you provoked Yahweh to wrath.
